# Itiha intelligence brief, 2026-11-15

**The Ramayana push is easing: long-form fell to 5,408 views on 2026-11-12, its lowest day since 4 November, and breakouts still stand at 0 this month. Three decisions follow: the Ravana fact-check long-form by 19 November, a Tipu Sultan Short for 20 November, and the Guru Tegh Bahadur Short for 24 November.**

## This week: 3 decisions
1. **Script and publish the Ravana fact-check long-form: who first argued that Ravana was the wronged side.** (long, due 2026-11-19, new)  
   Why: Three Ravana Shorts hold 73,838, 69,755 and 29,375 views with no long-form to send them to, and long-form converts 8.67x as well per view as Shorts over the 365-day window. The film window is closing.  
   First step: Outline it today: the British administrator's book of 1882 named in sentence one, then E. V. Ramasamy, then the film, ending on who repeats it now.
2. **Script, record and publish one Tipu Sultan Short for his birth anniversary on 20 November.** (short, due 2026-11-20, new)  
   Why: The moments radar's T-7 step is due now, the Karnataka row over Tipu Jayanti has been in the news for five days, and nothing is scripted. A dated moment with a live peg is the demonstrated route to a breakout.  
   First step: Choose one document from his own hand or his court and verify the quotation against the original before writing a line.
3. **Script and publish a Short on Aurangzeb's order to execute Guru Tegh Bahadur, for 24 November.** (short, due 2026-11-24, new)  
   Why: It is the highest-priority moment on the radar, the channel's two largest videos are Aurangzeb Shorts, and breakouts carry 66.5% of lifetime subscribers while this month's breakout lever stands at 0 against 823.  
   First step: Gather the named sources by 17 November and write sentence one as the order, the place and the date. An act of state, not a martyrdom story.

Everything below is the evidence. Mark a decision done or dropped on the Brief tab; an open one stays here until then.

## Channel health
17,400 subscribers against a target of 100,000 by 28 September 2027. November's milestone is 18,495, which needs 45.5 net a day; the 7-day rate is 47.9 and the 28-day rate 29.4. Projection basis: 7-day rate. On that basis the month ends at 18,118, 377 short, and the channel stands 367 behind the ramp today: just under it, not on it. Uploads now account for 63.1% of net subscribers over 28 days, so the rate rests mainly on videos. The lever furthest behind is breakouts, 0 against 823. 0.59 of a breakout at the median 1,393 subs. The demonstrated route is a newsjack of a mass release (Chhava gave three of four) or an evergreen controversy with a searchable name; check the calendar and news releases for the next peg. Long-form did 87,612 views in the last 7 days of Analytics against 64,381 the week before. Shorts did 143,881 against 72,929, most of it one Short over two days. Over 28 days long-form earned 63.5% of upload-attributed net subscribers.

What's working
- The best converter in the 90-day window is “How One Man Who Never Visited India Wrote Its History” at 12 net subscribers per 1,000: a named man convicted by his own record. Its verdict gives the shape for the Ravana long-form: “Name the villain, convict him with a document or payment he cannot deny, then end on who is still repeating him today.”
- “Why Does All of Asia Know the Ramayana?” has crossed the hit line of 65 net subscribers and carried the long-form lever to 258 this month against 113 targeted. It is 41.8% of all long-form views over the 365-day window.
- “Why Is Ram Setu Called ADAM'S Bridge?” is the best converter of the Ramayana-window Shorts, 1.2 per 1,000, and draws steady search every day. A title question answered with a dated map inside ten seconds is the search-side open to copy.

What's wrong
- Long-form reach is not becoming subscribers. The Asia video converts 2 net subscribers per 1,000 views and the Many Versions video 1.2. Part of that is the denominator: only 41.2% of November's long-form views were engaged views, so compare only with long-forms published since August, where these two are still among the three weakest. Probable cause: both open on a flat claim with no culprit on screen. Test: the Ravana long-form, culprit in sentence one, on the same film traffic.
- Both Ramayana long-forms leak at the same seam, around 0:31 to 0:35, where the hook hands off to a tour or a chronology. The verdict that names it: “A map is not a hook; the viewer needs a person with a grievance.” Test: in the Ravana long-form the minute after the hook stays with the hook's person; compare the drop at that point.
- Nothing made for the film window is built to convert. The four film Shorts convert between 0.2 and 0.6 net subscribers per 1,000, and the best-held converts worst, so retention is not the constraint. Probable cause: each answers one scene and ends. Test: the Tipu and Guru Tegh Bahadur Shorts told as complete stories at the longer length; compare per 1,000 on day three.
- “Itihasa vs Myth” has 73 public views and “Is Caste Unique to India?” 244 twelve days on, with days of zero in Analytics after publish, while a third clip from the same conversation has 1,752 in three days. Probable cause: they were not public, or were restricted, at launch. Test: check both in Studio.

## Audience
Analytics runs to 2026-11-12. Long-form is a Home-feed channel this month: 139,672 of 155,087 long-form views over 28 days came from the bucket that holds Home and the subscriptions feed, against 3,548 from search. Shorts drew 24.9% of their views from search over 28 days, so this month the feed carries them, not search.
- Two Wikipedia spikes are history demand: the Ramayana on English Wikipedia at 3.33x its 30-day median, and the Great Famine of 1876 to 1878 at 4.79x. The Nehru and Gandhi-family spikes are Children's Day and a memoir row: news, not evergreen demand.
- The month's Shorts search terms are Sai Pallavi and Ravana variants, then Ram Setu and Adam's Bridge, all landing on Shorts with no long-form behind them.
- WhatsApp referred 12,187 views over the 365-day window against Instagram's 441; the base is views referred from outside YouTube, a small part of all views. The most-forwarded videos are culprit-led long-forms, so seed the Ravana long-form there on day one.
- Niche comment activity peaks between 18:00 and 22:00 IST, strongest on Friday and Saturday. Publish an hour or two before it; the own sample is small, so treat it as a schedule to test.

## How they are reacting
The Ravana Shorts have moved the argument from the actress to the text: viewers are weighing the film's revenge motive against the epic's, and one says the film shows no scene of Ravana oppressing anyone. That is the opening a culprit-led fact-check needs. On the Asia long-form it is pride, plus a correction the script invited: the Cholas did send a fleet.
- **The film changed Ravana's motive** (mixed): "Maybe I'm oversimplifying this but the core reason for why he abducted Sita Ji is for lust and arrogance, now in Namit Malhotra's Ramayana they properly showed the arrogance part but replaced lust with revenge which leads to the controversy"
- **The film is soft on Ravana** (negative): "7:08 New movie is woke Ramayana, comrade Ravana freeing oppressed Rakshahas from Deva, they projected Lanka as communist utopia."
- **Pride in the Ramayana's reach across Asia** (positive): "Seriously 😳 even I'm not indian and Hindu , I'm a Burmese and Buddhist from my home country Myanmar but still big fan of Ramayana"
- **Correction: the Cholas did send an army** (mixed): "“Never sent a single soldier…” ever heard of Chola Empire?"
- **Not in our textbooks** (positive): "Wow, this was not even a footnote in our school history books."

Requested topics
- Rajendra Chola and Srivijaya, as the answer to “never sent a single soldier”
- A Krishna video in the same shape as the Asia Ramayana one
- The salt tax and the Yerukulas of Madras

## Competitors
Ten days after release the watchlist is still on the film, mostly with verdicts and reactions. Text against screen with a dated source is the lane Itiha's Ravana Shorts hold, and nobody on the list has made the long-form version. The Emissary has moved into the trade-route lane the Asia video opened.
- **Hindu Lifestyle**: "Diwali is South Asian... wait.. what?"
  Why it worked: 158,167 views at 31.7x, the top outlier of the last 30 days. It opens by quoting the claim it will knock down, then answers.
  Steal: Open on the opponent's sentence verbatim, then the reversal. Use it only where the answer is a document, not an opinion.
- **Upword**: "The Cost of Modernisation: Why Japan Abandoned Its 1,200-Year Beef Ban"
  Why it worked: 294,993 views at 14.1x, the strongest long-form outlier. A picture everyone holds, Wagyu as Japanese excellence, reversed by a dated act of government in January 1872.
  Steal: A held picture, then a dated act that contradicts it, inside the first 30 seconds. That is how the Ravana long-form should open.
- **Upword**: "An eight-year-old watched Ramayana and liked Ravan more than Shri Ram!"
  Why it worked: 23,171 views at 3.9x its median: one child's reaction stands in for a worry many parents share about the film's Ravana.
  Steal: The worry is the demand signal for the first decision. Answer where the sympathetic Ravana came from, with dates and names.

Gaps
- Ravana: three own Shorts and most of the month's Shorts search terms, with no long-form behind them; no competitor traces where the sympathetic Ravana came from.
- Direct Action Day: three own Shorts, steady monthly search, and no long-form.
- Flip queue: “Reality of Aurangzeb” (Mohak Mangal) has no source-led answer from any channel on the list. The 24 November Short answers it from the record, never as a reply.

## Trending now, make this
- **today, short, 3/5**: Great Famine of 1876 to 1878: Wikipedia spike  
  Signal: English Wikipedia's page is at 4.79x its 30-day median; the pack does not show the cause. Itiha's Temple Short on the same famine has 1,169 views and failed for want of a picture. (Wikipedia pageviews, own post-mortems)  
  Make: Not one of the three decisions. Only if a slot opens: a Short on Lord Lytton's imperial assemblage of 1 January 1877, held while the famine ran, with Lytton named in sentence one. A pageview spike lasts days, so after 17 November drop it.
- **this_week, short, 2/5**: Tarabai imprisons the Chhatrapati, 24 November 1750  
  Signal: The same day as the Guru Tegh Bahadur moment. Itiha's Tarabai Short is one of the four breakouts. The date comes from the on-this-day feed, so it is lower confidence. (Moments radar, own lifetime data)  
  Make: Second choice for 24 November, only after the Aurangzeb Short is recorded. Verify the date against a named source first.
- **watch, short, 2/5**: Constitution Day, 26 November  
  Signal: “Why Is Lord Rama in the Original Constitution of India?” went up on 13 November with a like rate of 9.2% against a Shorts median of 3.9%. (Calendar, own Analytics)  
  Make: Judge it on day three, 16 November. If it widens, a second Short on another illustration in the original document for 26 November.
- **watch, short, 2/5**: 4 December: “Maatrubhumi: May War Rest in Peace”, the next mass release  
  Signal: Its trailer is the most-viewed history-matched video on YouTube India's chart this week. The radar lists it as a war film; the pack does not say which war. The T-14 step opens on 20 November. (Moments radar, YouTube India chart)  
  Make: Find out by 20 November what it depicts. If it is a real event with a named antagonist, it becomes a decision next week: two Shorts scripted before release. Do not script from a trailer's framing.
- **watch, skip, 1/5**: Children's Day, Nehru and the Gandhi-family spikes  
  Signal: Nehru's Hindi Wikipedia page is at 23.84x its median and the hashtags lead X India, beside a row over a memoir. (X trends via getdaytrends, Wikipedia pageviews)  
  Make: Skip. A calendar day and a party-political row; contemporary politics is a rejected species and a news spike is not evergreen demand.

## Topic ideas (voltage-checked)
- [4/5, long] **Who Made Ravana the Wronged Hero? It Began With a British Book in 1882**  
  Decolonization reframe; Identity and religion stakes; Villain plus hypocrisy: a named author convicted from his own page; Contested history  
  source: Decision 1. Three own Ravana Shorts, the radar's fact-check step, Upword's Ravana outlier
- [3/5, short] **Aurangzeb's Order, Chandni Chowk, 1675: Why the Ninth Guru Was Executed**  
  Identity and religion stakes; Villain plus hypocrisy: a named emperor and a dated order; Contested history  
  source: Decision 3. Moments radar, flip queue
- [3/5, short] **Tipu Sultan History: What His Own Letters Say**  
  Identity and religion stakes; Contested history: the Karnataka row; The public picture against his own record  
  source: Decision 2. Moments radar, controversy news
- [3/5, long] **Direct Action Day: What Bengal's Chief Minister Did on 16 August 1946**  
  Identity, religion and nation stakes; Villain plus hypocrisy: a named chief minister; Contested history  
  source: Search gaps: three own Shorts and no long-form. The next long-form after Ravana

## Instagram (separate platform, separate audience)
Instagram has 25,313 followers, up 232 in 7 days. Carousels remain the growth format: median carousel reach is 7,078 against 1,882 for reels. The latest reel has a skip rate of 63.7% against a reel median of 54.2%; it opens on a promotion rather than a story.

Do more
- Write carousels in the revision lane  
  51 revision carousels in the band converted a median 53 followers against 22 for the other lanes (39 posts). Median reach 16.5k vs 12.5k, conversion 3.82 vs 2.12 per 1k.
- Build every carousel at 7-10 cards  
  The median carousel in the 7-10 band converts 37 followers (90 posts); outside the band, 12 (14 posts). Pooled rate 3.00 vs 1.51 follows per 1k reach — the band is not just reaching more people, it converts better per person reached, so this is not a reach artefact.

Do less
- Stop making posts that get shared without converting  
  17 of 102 rated posts are shared above the median (26.9/1k) but convert below it (2.2/1k): median 13.4k reach for a median 13 followers. The 34 posts that do both average 283 followers each. Share rate and follow rate correlate at only 0.39 — shareable and followable are separate skills, and the first one flatters itself on the home screen.
- Stop posting single images  
  86 single images all time: 74.9k reach between them and 103 followers, 1.2 per post. A carousel in the 7-10 band averages 161.4. Every image slot is a carousel slot not taken.

## Housekeeping
- **now**: Set the end screen and a pinned comment on both Ramayana long-forms to “How One Man Who Never Visited India Wrote Its History”.  
  It takes minutes and works on traffic the channel already has; the library tail is behind at 15 against 42.
- **this_week**: Check “Itihasa vs Myth” and “Is Caste Unique to India?” in Studio for visibility history and restrictions.  
  Days of zero views after publish suggest the first test never ran.
- **later**: Export Studio impressions and click-through for the two Ramayana long-forms.  
  Click-through exists only in Studio exports.
